ai.stableNodeKey: (outline) § subtitle#0

content.text: Client SDKs in the web and mobile apps send events to a collector service over HTTPS. Clients batch events and send them every 10 seconds, or sooner when the app goes to the background. Each event carries an event name, a timestamp, an anonymous device id and, for signed-in users, an account id.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Proposed design § text#0

content.text: The collector validates each event against the schema registry and rejects events that do not match a registered schema. Accepted events are published to the
analytics.events
topic on the message bus.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Proposed design § text#1

content.text: An enrichment step consumes the topic and adds account attributes, such as plan tier and region. The enrichment step uses the user service. If an account cannot be found, the event is passed on without account attributes.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Proposed design § text#2

content.text: Enriched events are then written to the warehouse in hourly batches, where the analytics team builds dashboards on them. The first dashboards will cover the onboarding funnel and weekly active accounts per plan tier.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Proposed design § text#3

content.text: We expect the user service to stay lightly loaded, so enrichment should avoid adding much traffic to it.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Proposed design § text#4

content.text: This design outlines an event analytics pipeline from client SDKs to a data warehouse, including event collection, validation, enrichment, and storage for dashboarding.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Next step § text#1

content.text: The growth team wants to understand how customers use the Lumen web and mobile apps. Today, product events are scattered across three logging tools, and nobody can answer a simple funnel question without exporting CSV files by hand. This proposal describes a single pipeline that collects product-analytics events, enriches them and makes them available in the warehouse. The first questions the team wants answered are how many new accounts finish onboarding, and which features paying customers use in their first month.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Context § P1

content.text: Every event type must be registered before clients can send it.
Schemas are versioned, and a breaking change requires a new version rather than an edit to the existing one.
Ownership of the schema registry has not been decided; the platform team and the data team have each suggested the other.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Schema registry § text#0

content.text: The schema registry is crucial for event type management, but its ownership remains an open decision between the platform and data teams.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Schema registry § text#1

content.text: Product managers want to see feature adoption in real-time, especially during launches.
Launch reviews typically occur within 2 hours of a release.
The current pipeline delivers events to the warehouse in real-time.
This ensures launch dashboards remain current.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Freshness § text#0

content.text: With this pipeline, events reach the warehouse in real time, so launch dashboards stay current.

ai.stableNodeKey: Proposal: product-analytics event pipeline (draft v0.3) › Freshness § text#1

content.text: Raw events are kept for 30 days, then deleted.
Only aggregated tables are kept longer.
Deleting raw events after a fixed period limits access request search scope.
Events must not contain email addresses or free-text input from users.
IP addresses are truncated by the collector before event publication.
